data.arc: June 2025 introduced a continent‑spanning heatwave that caused health impacts, infrastructure failures and fire warnings across Europe and rising heat risks in Asia. July 2025 saw the heatwave become deadly, with record deaths in Europe and the US, a nuclear plant shutdown, and widespread alerts and hose‑pipe bans. August‑October 2025 added massive wildfires, marine heat stress, and agricultural crises, culminating in December’s unprecedented heatwave that ignited record fires from Australia to Europe and generated over $120 billion in global economic losses. Early 2026 shifted toward intensified regional extremes—record‑breaking temperatures in southeast Australia and Europe, early US Southwest heat, and rising mortality risks in China—while scientific and policy responses emerged, including AI forecasts, safety standards, and EU calls for coordinated action. By May 2026 the heatwave became unseasonal and lethal across Western Europe and South Asia, underscoring a new normal of volatile, multi‑continent heat extremes.

Unprecedented global heatwave ignited record fires from Australia to Europe, leading to more than $120 billion in economic losses and deepening humanitarian crises.
Policy response emerged with a national safety standard to halt outdoor work during hazardous heat, and a large marine sponge experiment warned of potential mass die‑offs.
Record‑breaking heat across Europe and the UK prompted health alerts, a Met Office warning of accelerating 40 °C events, and new research linking heatwaves to rising heart disease risk.
Unseasonal heatwave produced record temperatures in Western Europe and South Asia, causing teenage deaths and over a hundred fatalities in India, signaling a new volatile normal.
